liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- ***Friend Of The Devil** (1 other source): Bob Weir played acoustic guitar on this song [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Easy Wind**: rare: 14 archived performances [10]
- **New Minglewood Blues**: rare: 14 archived performances [10]
- **Corrina**: rare: 4 archived performances [10]
- **Lost Sailor/Other One/Dark Star Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [10]
- **Jam/Drum Solo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [10]

## The recordings

- **dead2018-06-11.ccm4v.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 192 min [1]
- **deadandcompany2018-06-11.neumann-skm140.sunboy.flac24**: source not stated; 19 songs; 196 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the 24-bit transfer a very clean, solid audience recording, better suited to desk listening than car CDs [7]
- **deadandcompany2018-06-11.neumann_skm140.sunboy.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 196 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the taper's recordings very clean, solid audience recordings, praising the 24-bit version [8]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the crowd was good and the weather was perfect at the Saratoga show [5]
- At the end of the recording, a voice tells the taper he is one of the last ten tapers [7]
- At the recording's end, someone says the taper is one of the last ten tapers [8]
- Lineup was Mickey Hart, Bill Kreutzmann, Bob Weir, John Mayer, Oteil Burbridge and Jeff Chimenti [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **dead2018-06-11.ccm4v.flac16**: taped by Z-Man; source: Schoeps CCM4V's>Lunatec V2>Sound Devices 722 (24/44) [1]. Also: Recorded with Schoeps CCM4V microphones through Lunatec V2 into a Sound Devices 722 at 24-bit/44.1k, then converted to 16-bit FLAC; Taped from Section 8, Row CC, Seat 7, with microphones held 7.5 feet high [1]
- **deadandcompany2018-06-11.neumann-skm140.sunboy.flac24**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: Neumann SKM140(AK40's/LC3's/KM100's)>GAKables xlr>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/96>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/96kHz ~ [2]. Also: Taped from section 8, row HH, two rows behind the mixer enclosure, about four feet left of center, on a taper ticket [2]
- **deadandcompany2018-06-11.neumann_skm140.sunboy.flac16**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: Neumann SKM140(AK40's/LC3's/KM100's)>GAKables xlr>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/96>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/96kHz ~ [3]
